messages:
anna-sales: BrightPath wants a POC where PCI-scoped LLM requests are routed through their on-prem DLP appliance while non-PCI calls use Redwood hosted. Can we outline safe connectivity patterns + a one-page CISO responsibilities note by EOD?

rory-solutions: High-level patterns: 1) Customer-hosted reverse proxy (NAT passthrough) via VPC Peering/TGW -> preserves src-ip if configured. 2) PrivateLink interface endpoints to our connector, then customer-side proxy does TLS passthrough (more locked down but NATs client IP). 3) Hybrid: split by model route — sensitive models go to Private VPC with egress to customer proxy, others hit hosted.

jess-netops: Important netops asks from their team: no 0.0.0.0/0 outbound rules; need explicit Redwoods IP prefixes or interface endpoint DNS; retention of original client IP in logs for audit; and SNI exposure to their TLS-inspectors.

kai-security: If they want TLS MITM, they must supply certs and a signed chain we can accept. We prefer passthrough for POC to avoid entangling key management and increase time-to-test. Note: MITM may trigger additional data-handling controls.

rory-solutions: Quick firewall allowlist example for their team (keep minimal):
```
# POC allowlist (example)
- Dest: 13.59.0.0/16  # sample redwood-hosted-edge (provide exact CIDRs in handoff)
- Ports: 443 (TCP)
- SNI: allow *.redwood.ai (for SNI-based inspection)
- DNS: permit outbound DNS to customer resolver only (no public DNS)
```

anna-sales: Pricing/Q: Does PrivateLink create extra Redwood charges? Also what capacity bump if traffic is proxied back on-prem?

rory-solutions: AWS billing for interface endpoints is on the customer side (hours + data). Redwood charges a one-time private onboarding fee for Private deployments; for Hosted+proxy we may recommend a temporary Dedicated burst (pricing depends on burst size). I'll add a short estimate doc.

jess-netops: On src-ip preservation: PrivateLink will typically SNAT. If they must keep client IP we need a TCP passthrough NLB on their side with proxy-protocol v2 enabled and our connector configured to accept it. That requires ops work on both sides.

kai-security: For the CISO note: short paragraph I can send: "Routing PCI-sensitive model traffic through customer-controlled network controls ensures DLP and inspection occur inside your security boundary. Customer is responsible for certificate management, DLP configuration, firewall allowlists, and audit log retention for client identifiers. Redwood provides the private endpoint, guidance for NAT/passthrough options, and assists during the POC to validate connectivity and performance. Any on-path TLS interception increases compliance obligations and must be approved by both teams' security leads."

infra-bot: policy-checker: detected rule recommending open DNS egress. Suggest locking DNS to a known resolver or using AWS PrivateLink DNS integration.

rory-solutions: POC checklist (actionable):
- Customer: confirm CIDRs and SNI hostnames to permit
- Customer: decide on src-ip preservation requirement; if required provision NLB + proxy-protocol
- Customer: provide DLP proxy endpoint IPs and cert details if doing MITM (optional)
- Redwood: provision staging PrivateLink connector or peering route, enable route discrimination by model tag
- Redwood: schedule 15-min perf run with synthetic PCI payloads; measure latency and verify client id in logs
- Teams: security sign-off if MITM is chosen

anna-sales: Assignments: @rory-solutions to draft the Dedicated/burst estimate, @jess-netops to draft the minimal firewall snippet for handoff, @kai-security to finalize the CISO paragraph. I'll bundle and send to BrightPath tomorrow. :thumbsup:
